evidence.t: Mule deer winter range u-5-005 unit 14-225 (official), 40 m W. Counts from October.
Burn from 2023 (fire VA1664, 55 ha), 390 m N.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHws2): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
SE facing slope, 13 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from Village of Burns Lake, about 210 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 53.11059, -127.14844, pull off on Kimsquit Mainline FSR (paved road). Map links below.
Walk: 6.5 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 802 m, about 210 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m E of the spot at 626 m (53.14686, -127.07057). Water: Salahagen Creek 50 m NW (estimate).
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2023 burn (390 m N) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-9, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-02, closures 2026-10-16.
